title: Run JoinDependentFilterRule before DistributivityRule
summary: I moved the registration of JoinDependentFilterRule so it runs before DistributivityRule in src/optimizer/optimizer.cpp. This is a one-line move plus a comment. Now the rule sees the root OR before Distributivity pulls the shared join equality out of it. It returns AND(original OR, derived per-table ORs). Distributivity then still factors the join key out of the inner OR. On the next fixpoint pass the root is an AND, so the rule returns nullptr and there is no loop. EXPLAIN on my build shows the expected plan. The part scan now has a FILTER with the OR of the part predicates (2M -> 4,862 rows). The lineitem scan has the l_quantity OR range filter pushed in, and the shared shipmode/shipinstruct filters are still pushed. Join output dropped from 2.14M to 2,672 rows, and join time from 0.87s to 0.01s. bench: q19 went from 336.1 ms to 157.0 ms (-53.3%), and results matched.
notes: The expression rewriter runs only once per optimization (optimizer.cpp RunOptimizer EXPRESSION_REWRITER), so later passes cannot derive the filters twice. I did not need the fallback (extending Apply to a root AND). Only q19 was benchmarked. I did not run the existing optimizer tests (they are outside the dbe-tool commands I can use). Plans may now differ, with extra derived filters, for other queries whose OR branches share common terms.

title: Linear-time union in scan ConjunctionOr filter
summary:
The issue's hypothesis was wrong. The lineitem OR-of-ranges filter is not a ConjunctionOrFilter. FilterCombiner::TryPushdownOrClause only builds ConjunctionOrFilter for an OR of plain comparisons, so an OR of BETWEEN/AND ranges is pushed as an EXPRESSION_FILTER and runs through ExpressionExecutor::SelectExpression. Replacing the quadratic union in CONJUNCTION_OR alone (the plan as written) moved the isolated scan only 2.62s→2.39s cumulative.

All changes are in src/storage/table/column_segment.cpp:
1. New dense-mask path (TryDenseFilterSelection), used by both EXPRESSION_FILTER and CONJUNCTION_OR. It applies when the column is numeric (int8..int128, uint8..uint128, float, double), the vector is flat (vdata.sel unset), and the filter is a tree of AND/OR over comparisons (=, <>, <, >, <=, >=) and BETWEEN between the column itself (BOUND_REF index 0, same type) and non-NULL constants of exactly the column type. Each comparison becomes one branchless loop writing a 0/1 mask, AND/OR combine the masks, and the selection is emitted in input order. If the incoming sel is non-identity, the selected values are gathered into a compact buffer first. NULL rows are dropped at the end via validity, which is correct because the tree has no NOT. Anything else falls through to the existing code.
2. CONJUNCTION_OR fallback: the O(n²) duplicate-check union is replaced by a per-row bool bitmap. Later children only see rows not yet matched, and the output keeps input order. This only applies when all sel indices are < STANDARD_VECTOR_SIZE; otherwise the old loop runs (scan_count can exceed the vector size).

Measured with dbe-tool on my build:
- Isolated `count(*) WHERE OR of 3 ranges`: scan 2.32s→0.97s cumulative, 0.305s→0.134s wall. That is now the same cost as a single BETWEEN (0.97s).
- bench q19: −7.3% and −11.3% on two runs (155→144ms, 163→145ms).
- An intermediate version without the gather (masking all 2048 rows even with a sparse incoming sel) was +5.2% slower on q19 on two runs. The gather fixed that.
- bench result checks passed on every run.
notes:
- Profile ToString looks the same for ConjunctionOrFilter and ExpressionFilter. Check which TableFilterType actually reaches FilterSelection before optimizing it.
- In the scan, the OR filter often runs after more selective filters (shipinstruct eq, the bloom-filter dynamic filter), so work must stay proportional to the incoming sel. Dense evaluation of the full vector cost +5%; gathering first fixed it.
- Possible follow-up: make TryPushdownOrClause build ConjunctionOr-of-ConjunctionAnd TableFilters for OR-of-ranges. That would also enable zonemap pruning through ConjunctionOrFilter::CheckStatistics, but it is a riskier plan-level change.
- The remaining lineitem scan cost in q19 is the other filters: the string-equality filter, the optional IN filter on another string column, and the bloom-filter dynamic filter.

title: Dictionary-level filter evaluation for Dictionary-compressed string segments
reasons: abandoned by the implementer after investigation
summary:
I implemented the change, but it made q19 no faster. bench q19 went from 116.6 ms to 115.9 ms (-0.6%, which is noise), so I'm abandoning it.

What I built: a `filter` callback for plain Dictionary-compressed VARCHAR segments, in dictionary_compression.cpp, ported from DictFSSTFilter.
- It evaluates the filter once per dictionary entry and caches a bool per entry. Slot 0 (NULL) is evaluated only when a row actually references it.
- Rows are mapped through the bitpacked selection that ScanToDictionaryVector produces, so the output stays a dictionary vector.
- To avoid a header change, the cache lives in a scan-state subclass defined in the .cpp.
- Guards: full vectors only, dictionary size at most STANDARD_VECTOR_SIZE, and the filter tree must have a stable result (constant, IS [NOT] NULL, IN, non-volatile expression, AND/OR/OPTIONAL of those). Anything else uses the old scan-then-filter path.
- In numeric_constant.cpp, ConstantFun::FiltersNullValues now handles IN_FILTER and DYNAMIC_FILTER by keeping all rows instead of throwing.

The tree builds. I ran no result checks beyond what `bench q19` does.

The key measurement was an A/B on the same build, with the callback switched off and on, for `count(*) WHERE <dictionary varchar> = const` (cumulative scan time):
- Single filter: 0.56s with the old path, 0.59s with the new one.
- Plus a numeric OR-of-ranges filter: 0.93s old, 1.12s new.

The issue's 1.14s figure for the isolated filter did not reproduce on the current build. Comparing strings row by row through the dictionary selection is already cheap, and the fast path is the same speed or slightly slower.
notes:
- The cost model was wrong. Even a filter that passes every row on the Dictionary column (`col >= ''`) costs about 0.46s cumulative over 60M rows. The filter that rejects 75% costs 0.56–0.59s. So the time goes into per-vector scan overhead (the row-group filter loop, the validity filter, pinning or segment handling), not into the string compares.
- The q19 lineitem scan costs 2.68s cumulative in my profile, not the 3.38s quoted in the issue.
- A cheaper first check for this kind of idea is a same-build on/off comparison of the isolated predicate.
- The optional `l_shipmode IN` filter is shown on the scan but does not seem to be applied per row: 7.5M rows come out of the scan, and the FILTER operator above it does the work, costing 0.09–0.18s.
- Possible follow-ups:
  - Profile per-vector scan overhead with perf on a filter that passes every row.
  - Check whether optional IN filters on dictionary columns could be applied in the scan (that would need the adaptive-filter or optional-filter policy).
- Saved in memory as dictionary-filter-no-gain.

title: Skip all-optional ConjunctionAnd table filters in the scan filter loop
reasons: abandoned by the implementer after investigation
summary: I made no code change. I profiled q19.m0 on the current best before touching anything. The lineitem TABLE_SCAN lists only one optional filter on the shipmode column: `optional: l_shipmode IN ('AIR', 'AIR REG')`. A ConjunctionAnd prints its children joined with " AND ", and this line has none, so the filter is a single top-level OPTIONAL_FILTER. RowGroup::CheckZonemap (row_group.cpp:626) already marks that kind of filter always-true and skips it. The AND-of-optionals the issue describes (IN plus OR-of-equals on the same column) is not produced for q19 on the current engine. The issue's A/B microbench only created it by adding an extra OR predicate to the query. Since the cost isn't in the q19 profile, the change would have no effect there.
notes: The only AND of optionals in the q19 lineitem scan is in the dynamic filters on l_partkey (`optional >= AND optional <= AND optional BF`). Those are SelectivityOptionalFilter (min/max and Bloom filter) and really do filter, so the planned skip rightly leaves them alone. The scan takes 5.84s of operator time (cumulative over threads); total query time is 0.786s. Better places to look for q19 scan time are the BF/min-max dynamic filter cost on l_partkey, the expression-filter evaluation of the l_quantity OR-of-ranges, and the shipinstruct equality on a Dictionary/FSST column. The upper FILTER on the shipmode OR takes 0.12s. Before planning around an AND-of-optionals, check the current profile.

title: Cost-aware initial scan filter order: run Bloom/dynamic join filters after cheap constant predicates
reasons: abandoned by the implementer after investigation
summary:
I tried the cost-aware initial scan filter order and abandoned it because bench shows no measurable gain on q19. The tree builds.

Changes in ExpressionHeuristics::Cost(const TableFilter&):
- BLOOM_FILTER costs 50.
- SelectivityOptionalFilter takes its child's cost (plain OptionalFilter stays 0).
- EXPRESSION_FILTER takes Cost(expr) instead of 1000.
- Fixed the BOUND_REF case in Cost(Expression&). It cast a BoundReferenceExpression to BoundColumnRefExpression, and Cast throws even in release builds.

Results:
- Steps (1)+(2) alone: bench q19 +3.0%, so no effect.
- With (3) added, the Bloom filter now runs after the cheap predicates. In the q19.m0 profile the lineitem scan's cumulative time fell from 5.88s to 4.70s, and total time from 0.792s to 0.651s.
- Bench q19 over five runs: -5.9%, -3.2%, +9.4%, +2.3%, +1.7%. That is within noise; wall time did not improve.
notes:
- Filter ordering is not the bottleneck for q19's lineitem scan. The profile gain did not show up in bench wall time.
- Bench noise on q19 is about ±10% between runs. The baseline itself moved between 128 and 174ms.
- Latent bug: ExpressionHeuristics::Cost(Expression&) BOUND_REF does Cast<BoundColumnRefExpression>(), which throws InternalException. Any future change that sends ExpressionFilter expressions (which contain BoundReferenceExpression) through Cost must fix that case first.
- In the profile with the change, the plan showed the shipmode optional filter twice ("optional: l_shipmode IN (...) AND optional: l_shipmode IN (...)"). It is probably a re-planning or pushdown artefact, not caused by this change, but it may be worth checking.
- Next things to look at: per-row decode and Bloom-filter probe cost, not ordering.

title: Skip pure-optional ConjunctionAnd scan filters (zonemap-only) in the per-row filter loop
reasons: abandoned by the implementer after investigation
summary:
I'm abandoning this one: the change builds and works but made q19 no faster (144.9 ms → 144.6 ms, -0.2%, within noise).

What I changed: in src/storage/table/row_group.cpp I added a static helper, IsZonemapOnlyFilter. It returns true for a plain OptionalFilter (it excludes SelectivityOptionalFilter with a dynamic_cast) and for a CONJUNCTION_AND whose children are all such filters, checked recursively. RowGroup::CheckZonemap now also marks those filters always-true. The existing handling of a top-level OPTIONAL_FILTER is unchanged and no headers were touched.

The profile after the change still shows the filters on the lineitem scan. The scan still outputs 82,782 rows, so the dynamic join filters on the join key (an AND of SelectivityOptionalFilters) still filter rows as before.
notes: The hypothesis that this no-op filter costs a full decode of the dictionary column was wrong for this query. The no-op filter on the ship-mode column runs after the selective quantity and shipinstruct filters, which keep only about 0.14% of rows. Filtering a Dictionary column outputs dictionary vectors cheaply, so the no-op pass costs very little. The ~0.46s figure from E0003 does not carry over here. Scan cumulative time was 4.86s in this profile, versus 5.84s in the issue's profile, but that is from a different run and the timed bench shows no difference. Do not retry skipping no-op per-row optional filters on dictionary columns. The remaining scan cost is probably in decoding the filter columns themselves (quantity, shipinstruct) and in the join-key Bloom filter.
